name: 2033 Prairie Avenue — Otis Italianate rowhouse (district draft; refined by T-1918)

function.note: The 1911 sheet marks the building 'D' (dwelling): '3B brick dwelling with a stone front and a full-height bay (D), the middle house of the row'. Carried to 1904 on the T-1842 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

research_note: A DISTRICT DRAFT (T-2352, the owner's district pass of 2026-10-08): a serviceable first model, complete from the street, the walks, the alley and the air, that T-1918 refines in place under this same id. Written by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py from the sheet 35 trace (s35fp-2033-b1), the T-1842 census (s35-2033-front, s35-2033-wing) and the T-1837 register row frontage-35-082 (Otis Italianate rowhouse); every height, roof, opening and feature is the draft rules' reconstruction (data/components/prairie_1904/draft_prairie_1904.json; liberty L-draft-prairie-20-22-east-2352).

documented_range.note: The draft claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-1842 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Its building and loss dates are the per-building ticket's to read.

position.symbolic_location: 2033 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_2033 (data/street_grid/1904.json), east side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 20th to 22nd Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 35).
position.note: The rear corner of the main body's rectangle (lot frame u 33.750, v -3.000 m from the middle of the rear lot line), through the T-1250 fit of the sheet: the sheet's georeference carries no independent check: its own fit residual is 0.05 m RMS on its control crossings, a similarity on two degrees of freedom that says little away from them, plus about a pixel (0.19 m) of trace on this coarser copy. Rotation 179.385 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line.

derivation.reason: The four derivation methods re-derive from the 1835 files; this position is re-derived from the traced sheet and the 1904 parcel by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py --check instead.

footprint.note: The main body: the largest rectangle that fits inside the traced main part (u toward the street, v along the front). The building's other rectangles are in draft_plan.

stories.note: '3B; rear2B' printed on the 1911 sheet: 3 full storeys.

draft_plan.note: Rectangles fitted inside the traced parts by the rules' fit (cell 0.25 m, at most 3 a part, to 90% cover): s35fp-2033-b1 p2 (main, brick), rectangle 1 of that part; the part's rectangles cover 82% of its fill; s35fp-2033-b1 p2 (main, brick), rectangle 2 of that part; the part's rectangles cover 82% of its fill; s35fp-2033-b1 p1 (range, stone), rectangle 1 of that part; the part's rectangles cover 62% of its fill. Storeys per piece and roof per piece are the draft rules' (reconstructed).

draft_elevation.note: RECONSTRUCTED by the draft rules, family row 'Italianate' overlaid with the frontage row: 2033, the Otis homestead in the middle of the 1869 limestone row (Tribune, February 1904): the row's bracketed flat cornice over three storeys and the sheet's full-height canted stone bay, which the fit carries as a bay; the pedimented double-door hood the Walker Evans photograph shows is T-1918's. Heights are the rules' starting values inside RECONSTRUCTION-RULES.md's ranges; bays, entrance side, chimneys and dormers are counts the family rules choose, and the seed 3843080768 only tints the fabric inside +-6 %.
